calls.text: Round 3 started 23:31:57 UTC on 2026-11-23. No time limit this round; a status goes into the thread at least every 30 minutes.

Round 2 was moved whole to references/archive/round-2/ and pushed (e327a49) before anything else. Nothing from rounds 1 or 2 is reused: no image, take, prompt, layout study or real photograph. Workspace tooling for this round is written new.

Hardest place chosen for Step 1: The Breath. It is the only one of the six that is an action rather than a shape, so it has to be invented, still read as part of a body, be walkable and be deadly. The Ribs, Spine and Eye already have a silhouette to start from.

Three film-wide directions, each a rule that generates all six places. A Overgrowth: the titan lies under rainforest, anatomy survives as landform, warm wet daylight in shafts, the forest kills. B Titan-fall: the body is still being eaten, nothing is a plant, life is animal colonies and scavengers, cold sea light, the chemistry kills. C Corpse-light: permanent dusk, the land is dark, every light is alive and is bait.

Batch 1 (15 takes, 3 models, eye-level and low-drone variants) was a probe of first designs: A as a forest of ringed airway trees, B as a tidal shelf of exhaling throats, C as a ribbed gorge with glow threads and floating bell animals.

Lessons from batch 1: (1) never describe the camera as an object, two takes drew it; (2) A's ringed airway trees look like hoses, so A is redesigned as the inside of the windpipe: a tunnel cave with collapsed skylights and a forest island under each shaft of sun; (3) B is the closest to a real place but drifts toward the grey of round 1, so the shelf gets broad crimson colonies, a warmer low sun and a far goal (the broken main windpipe); (4) C's ribbed gorge clashes with The Ribs and its animals are Earth jellyfish, so C is redesigned as a valley of living air sacs glowing from inside at dusk.

Critic calibration set 1: three blind critics from three model families (GPT-6.2 Sol, Gemini 4 Carbon, Claude Opus 5.5) each get eight stills in mixed order with no context: my three first candidates, three round 2 kept images (Breath take 1, Ribs take 4, Eye take 3) as negative controls, and two real photographs (Son Doong cave, Cape Bridgewater blowholes, both Wikimedia Commons CC BY-SA) as positive anchors. The rubric is only trusted if it puts round 2 at the bottom and the photographs at the top. Round 2 images go to critics only, never to a generator.

Calibration result: the rubric is valid. All three blind critics ranked both photographs first, my three candidates in the middle, and all three round 2 images last, in the same order (Ribs, Breath, Eye). Mean place score: photographs 9.5, round 3 candidates 6.6, round 2 images 3.4. So the critics see the fault the user saw in round 2, and they also say round 3 is not yet at the level of a real place. Shared faults to remove: cloned repeats (vents, skylights, domes), animals posed in a row, flocks pasted on, one hero prop in the foreground, far landmarks that look built. I use this rubric from here on and always include a photograph and a round 2 image as controls.

Decision after critic rounds 2 and 3: the route and the stations now work (all critics describe a path with three stops in every round 3 frame), but the frames are crowded and repeat one object many times, and the animals are too big, which destroys scale. Change of approach for the establishing views, not another re-shoot of the same frame: (1) land first, life small: animals become the scale cue, like the caver in the Son Doong photograph, and the richness moves into the detail views; (2) fewer motifs, wide plain areas of rock, water and fog; (3) life in zones (bands at the waterline, rings at the rims) instead of dressing every surface; (4) one light source, backlit, so vapour glows and near faces fall into shadow; (5) a slightly raised viewpoint so more ground plane and route are visible; (6) every repeated thing differs in size, state and angle.

Batch 6 (restraint pass) reviewed: new establishing picks A take 21, B take 21, C take 22. They go to a fourth blind packet against three photographs and two round 2 images before any detail is re-shot.

Packet 4 (two of three critics in): the restraint pass worked for A (9 and 9, called a film frame, level with the photographs) and C (8 and 7, film frame). B still reads as a painting (8 and 6). Change of approach for B: throats become shafts flush with the ground, one accent colour only, a far flock of small waders replaces the row of big striders, sun out of frame, smooth wave-cut rock. A and C get one more re-shoot against the listed faults.

Packet 4 complete. Sol and Opus now put A level with the photographs (9, film frame) and C just under (8, 7, film frame); Carbon, the hardest critic in every packet, still calls all three paintings (A 4, B 5, C 6). Critics disagree on A. Carbon's valid points taken: corner foreground props read as a 2D frame, skylights on one axis, animals in profile. The foreground props move out of the corners into the scene.

Blind packets 5 and 6 (two critics in so far): A and B now rated film frames at 8 to 9 by Sol; Opus split (film in packet 6, painting in packet 5) at 6 to 7; C still painting at 6 to 7 with both. Ran edit 4 against the named faults: A one light source and half-buried hoops; B ragged shaft, crimson in three zones, ragged cave; C matte ground, varied sacs, lit cave interior.

B edit 4 fixed the machined look but lost the anatomy (hoops read as rock ledges, waders as flamingos). Running edit 5 to put irregular organic hoops back and make the waders four-legged: the place must stay impossible as well as believable.

Blind packets 7 and 8 on the edit 4 to 6 re-shoots: no gain. A holds (Sol film frame 9 three times running, Opus 5 to 6). B fell from 9 to 8 to 7 with Sol as the chain of re-shoots grew a repeating crackle texture on the rock; C the same (over-sharpened, gravel smearing). Chained re-shooting has stopped paying: stop it, go back to the cleanest generation of each (A take 30, B take 34, C take 29) and change approach for any further gain.

Change of approach (chained re-shoots had stopped improving and were adding a crackle texture): fresh 'plate' generations. Each gets two references with separate jobs: a public-domain real photograph as the rendering standard only (Hoh rainforest mist for A, Great Fountain terraces at sunset for B, Halemaumau at dusk for C) and a small blurred copy of the chosen frame as layout only, so every surface is invented fresh. Prompt adds what the critics kept naming: plain surfaces, small unposed animals, one light, no sun disc. Three models per direction (Sunburst x2, Seedream 5 x2, Nano Banana 2.1 x1), 15 takes.

Fresh plates work: all three directions now read as location photography. New establishing picks: A-est-t41, B-est-t55 (plate v2, hoops as windpipe rings), C-est-t41. Details re-made from the new plates with the same two-reference method; first results (waders, grazers, spore bladders, the snared animal) are the strongest frames of the round. C-d1 take 12 showed a caught animal with a hand that could be read as a person, so the prey was changed to a four-legged young animal. Blind packet 9 launched on the three new plates.

Packet 9 (first blind scores for the fresh plates): Sol A 8 / B 8 / C 7, Opus 7 / 8 / 8, Carbon 4 / 6 / 5; photographs 7 to 10, round 2 frames 1 to 5. All three still name faults I can fix in the prompt (proscenium frame and twin tusks in A; smooth concentric hoops, waders in a row, flat cave in B; sacs at staged intervals with no bounce light in C). One more fresh plate per direction (b20), then details re-made from the new plates (b21).

Build opinions on the nine stills (two engineers, estimates only, not measurements): Sol MATCH A 6 / B 8 / C 7, rank B, C, A; Opus MATCH A 3 / B 5 / C 5, rank C, B, A. Both put A last (dense foliage, close animal skin). They split on B against C.

Blind packet 10 complete: all three critics label the three new plates FILM except Sol on C (PAINTING); PLACE scores A 9/7/9, B 8/8/9, C 8/8/9 (Sol/Opus/Carbon) against 7 to 10 for the real photographs. Same-location test 2 (Sol, Opus so far): all six details assigned to the right wide, confidence 7 to 10. Named continuity faults: A herd reads as elephants in the wide but as long-necked eyeless grazers in the detail; B rim carcass reversed in the detail and the standing wader missing; C middle sac ribbed in the wide but smooth in the detail and the cave missing. Call: one last targeted batch (b22): one-step revision of plate A (herd) and plate C (star-shaped moths), re-shoot of B detail 1 and C detail 2 for continuity. Swap in only if better at full size.

Final polish batch b22 judged at full size. Swaps: plate A t53 -> t55 (herd now the same animals as the detail), plate C t50 -> t56 (moths, light spill), B detail 1 t21 -> t32 (carcass the same way round as the wide, rim wader added), C detail 2 t21 -> t31 (ribbed sac, cave behind). Blind packet 10 and same-location test 2 scored the earlier versions; packet 11 and same-location test 3 re-test the final nine.

Blind packet 11 (final plates): Sol A 9 / B 9 / C 8, all FILM; Opus A 7 / B 8 / C 8, all FILM; Carbon A 4 / B 5 / C 6, all PAINTING. Real photographs 6 to 10; round 2 frames 1 to 6. Carbon does not agree with itself between runs: the identical plate B scored 9 FILM in packet 10 and 5 PAINTING in packet 11. Reported as received.

Same-location test 3 (final nine): all three critics placed all six details in the correct wide view (18 of 18). Sureness 7 to 10. One coherent place: B YES, YES, MOSTLY; C MOSTLY, YES, MOSTLY; A MOSTLY, MOSTLY, MOSTLY (Opus, Sol, Carbon; Sol sent two replies, the later one is used). Named breaks kept in NOTES.md for step 2.

Gap found at hand-over: the six detail views were only ever tested for being the same place as their wide view, never blind-scored for realism. Running blind packets 12 (three detail-1 views) and 13 (three detail-2 views), each with three real animal photographs and two round 2 frames, three fresh critics each. Rule fixed before seeing results: a detail passes if at least two of three critics label it PHOTO or FILM and the mean REAL score from Sol and Opus is 7 or more; it fails if two or more critics call it PAINTING or AMATEUR or that mean is 5 or less; anything between is reported as borderline. A failed detail gets one fresh re-generation round and one retest.

Blind packets 12 and 13 (the six details, REAL 0-10 and source label; Sol / Opus / Carbon): A-d1 FILM 8 / FILM 6 / PAINTING 4; A-d2 FILM 8 / FILM 6 / AMATEUR 5; B-d1 FILM 7 / FILM 6 / FILM 5; B-d2 FILM 7 / FILM 5 / AMATEUR 4; C-d1 FILM 7 / FILM 5 / FILM 6; C-d2 FILM 7 / FILM 6 / AMATEUR 6. Real animal photographs 10 from every critic; round 2 frames 1 to 6. By the rule fixed beforehand: A-d1 and A-d2 pass (mean 7.0), the four B and C details are borderline (6.0 to 6.5), none fails. Named tells: waxy or rubbery creature skin, water drips as tidy lines of beads, regular slit rows, staged carcass and pair, veins drawn on the sac surface, moths pasted, threads without tension. My own check at full size of B-d2 and A-d2: Carbon's limb-count faults are occlusion misreads, the drip lines and slit rows are real tells. Decision: the brief says keep going until every image can be defended, so one revision round on all six details with a changed approach (a real photograph of real animal skin or tissue as the standard, and the named tells listed as the only changes), then one retest. If it does not lift them, the originals stay and the finding is reported.

User message at about 01:56 UTC: quality is up to par, but the run is taking far too long; wants a handful of pictures from each environment, everything made so far and what is left; do not stop working. Applied: the detail polish round (batch 23) is not pursued further and no more blind packets are run before moving on; step 2 starts now in direction B, Titan-fall (my recommendation), stated as the default the user can overrule at any time; method cut down to my own eye plus at most one non-blocking critic pass; every place shown inline as soon as it exists.

02:23 Detail takes b26-b28 all returned (44). Chosen by eye from full-size views. One redo only: eye iris mats (both takes put thumb-sized grazers that read as miniature lambs beside bubbles their own size, which makes the lake read small). Changed approach: no animals on the mats, scale set by an adult drinker standing among filaments longer than it is. Marsh thin-crust: take 2 kept over take 1 because take 1 gave the wallower an eye and the establishing view has them eyeless. Eye edge: take 2 kept over take 1 because take 1 puts a skull with an eye socket in the foreground.

02:38 Final check of the set against my own rule that nothing living in the film has eyes or ears (the only eye is the dead one). Three details break it or drift from their place's animal: ribs detail 2 (the near kite-wing has an eye), eye detail 2 (the drinker reads as a horse), eye detail 4 (the two foreground drinkers have ears and wool). One single-step fix each (batch 30, two takes each), swapped in only if better at full size; otherwise the originals stay with the fault stated.

02:41 Batch 30 judged at full size. All three fixes swapped in: ribs-d3c-t1 (eye removed, nothing else changed), eye-d2c-t2 (horse replaced by the drinker of detail 1), eye-d4c-t2 (ears and wool removed). Remaining stated fault on eye detail 4: from behind the blunt heads read as plain stumps.

REVEAL REDO (user message, about 02:58 UTC). Direction B approved for all six places, kept exactly as they are. Only the reveal is rejected: 'reads as a fish with arms growing out of its head; the skull and one hand are bunched together at one end and nothing else says human'. New brief: a humanoid titan unmistakable at a glance (head, shoulders, both arms, rib cage, spine, hips, both legs, human proportions), on its back or slightly on its side, limbs spread, a landmass at continental scale and not a statue or a clean skeleton, seen from almost directly above with the curve of the planet only at the edge of frame; the six places findable and looking like themselves from orbit; a pull-back in four key frames from the same rising camera (lake, skull massif, head and shoulders, whole titan) that agree with each other and hold real scale; tested with fresh agents told nothing. Start new, reuse nothing of the old reveal but the idea. Old reveal moved to references/archive/round-3-reveal/ (kept image, sheet, three takes, prompt, the two ISS plates used for it).

Fresh-viewer protocol fixed before results (critic/fresh/PROTOCOL.md): viewers are new agents on separate machines, several models, one image with a meaningless file name, told nothing. GLANCE = picture at 400 px and one open question, as the stand-in for 'within two seconds' (the human two-second read itself stays UNKNOWN). FULL = five questions on size, camera, medium and features. Pass rules written down first.

Reveal redo, new start. Pose: on its back, head left, feet right, one arm raised, one knee bent, so that the outline reads at once and no two limbs lie alike. Seen from almost straight above, the planet's edge only at the top left.
First body: 24 takes on five procedural layout maps (rv4), 03:27 to 03:48. rv4-t23 chosen.

Pull-back built on rv4-t23 by re-photographing windows of it from closer (masters v1 to v8; takes pb3, tile, pb2, pb1, bl, fl, fu, hl, hu, cs, sm), 03:51 to 06:02. Tested six times on fresh viewers (a1 to ag3) and rebuilt each time: side-on head read as an animal and was replaced by a face-up skull; storm, sea specks, belly and neck join reworked.

User note: 'One update currently it looks like the Titan is just laying down in the ocean. I don't know if I love that. He doesn't look deep composed or creepy enough.' Read as 'decomposed'; applied without asking. The whole first body is dropped with its eight masters. New rule: the outline says corpse, the surface says continent. STATE brief added so that 'creepy' is measured against the old body as baseline.

The carcass: 14 takes from text and real orbital photographs only (cx), 06:12 to 06:20. Viewers flagged the first ones as sculpted, so they were re-photographed toward real orbital photography. cx-t9 chosen.

Master built on cx-t9 (master-c1, then master-x1 with more ocean round it) and tested (ao1 to ar3). The skeleton reads at once. Corrections the tests asked for: shoulder joints and collar bones, plainer limbs with hands and feet, a through-going strait between two rows of ribs, the storm on the backbone, a whiter salt pan.

Those corrections painted onto master-x1 as a layout (tools/guide_e.py, guide/cx-e-guide.png) and the wide picture made again from it: cx-e, three takes. cx-e-t2 chosen by eye and tested (as1 to au4) before anything was built on it.

Set x2: 21 closer plates of cx-e-t2 (e2), joined into master-x2 (tools/master.py); Heart lights added by script (tools/heart_x2.py); frame 1 plate pb1d. Tested (av1 to bc2): GLANCE 3 of 3, FULL 6 of 6, but the head reads as carved and the storm as an eruption or explosion to 4 of 6.
Set x4: head and storm re-photographed (e3-HD, five takes, takes 2 to 5 each tested on three viewers, take 4 kept; e3-ST-t1 kept), new frame 1 plate pb1e-t1. Tested (bi1 to bp2).

Set x5: frame 3 of x4 drew 'a giant fish skeleton' from one viewer of three and 'fish-bone or feathers' from a second. Three other windows tested on nine new viewers (bq1 to bs3); window D adopted, by my choice on their answers.

Set x6: PROPORTION test on x5 (bt1 to bt3) says head too big 3 of 3. Head reduced to 0.66 and neck lengthened by one smooth warp of the master (tools/headwarp.py, tag c). Frame 2 drawn through the warp so the tested head is kept pixel for pixel; the sea round it re-photographed once (pb2g-t2) and merged outside a head mask (tools/f2_merge.py). master-x6.

x6 tested on 26 new viewers (bu1 to cb2): GLANCE 3 of 3, FULL 6 of 6, STATE 4, 4, 4, PLACES 6, 5, 6 of 6, head right 2 of 3 and slightly too big 1 of 3. Decision: stop here and hand over. The waist reads too long to 3 of 3 in the PROPORTION test; it is left as it is because that stretch of backbone is The Spine and carries the storm. Offered to the user as an option.

Record faults found and mended: prompts/pb2-g.txt had been overwritten at 08:10 with the new frame 2 prompt (now prompts/pb2-x6.txt); the original text was restored word for word from the session record. Ten replies of the x4 round that had not been saved to file were restored word for word from the session record (bp2 is cut at 4,000 characters there and is marked so).

eye.text: Darkest and most photographic of the five, but the airway trees read as giant ribbed hoses lying in a wood; the design is the problem, not the take.
A cinema camera on a tripod stands in the frame (the model drew my viewpoint sentence literally). Orange glowing fruit, illustration look.
Best surface texture of the set, but golden glowing sacs and soft god rays make it fantasy key art.
Good restraint and depth, same hose problem.
Stylised CG illustration: outsized sacs, clean ribbed tubes.
Reads as a real place: channel, receding vents, far arch. Palette close to grey; one hero throat in the foreground.
Bright CG look, feather-like plumes, walkers read as people and horses.
Most photographic take of the batch: wet weed, lichen, real tidal light, walkers and flock at depth. Low resolution (1672x941) and the nearest throat still dominates as a hero object.
Best layout of the batch (winding channel, vents at many distances) but nearly monochrome grey; tall stumps read as chimneys.
CG render look; stumps read as smokestacks.
Restrained and dark, but the walls are a rib cage (clashes with The Ribs) and the animal is an Earth jellyfish.
Fantasy illustration; Earth jellyfish.
Best texture, still a fantasy poster: big jellyfish, glowing bead curtain filling the right side.
Too dark to read; rib-cage walls.
A drone is drawn in the frame; rib-cage walls.

Batch 2 pick for A. Ribbed tunnel, skylight island, river: reads as a place. Faults: foreground bladders are giant white eggs and a hero prop; plants and flyers are Earth plants and birds; nothing shows how it kills.

crit.text:
v1 | FILM | PLACE 9 | ROUTE: Skim the foreground water channel, bank past the long-legged animal on the steaming sinkhole rim, then cross the flats toward the enormous cave in the escarpment. | FAULTS: Several waders repeat the same head-down silhouette; their needle-thin feet and the prone animal’s splayed limbs are hard to read against the rock.
v2 | PHOTO | PLACE 10 | ROUTE: Drop past the nearer left flowstone to the lit boulders beside the tiny caver, climb around the central stalagmite cluster, then peer into the dark passage to its right. | FAULTS: none.
v3 | AMATEUR | PLACE 6 | ROUTE: Slip between the close icy trunks, track beside the bison-like herd crossing the glade, then drift into the faint trees behind it. | FAULTS: The two sides frame the sky almost symmetrically; bark shines like clear plastic, the herd repeats in side profile, and the uniform mist turns the deeper woods into a backdrop.
v4 | FILM | PLACE 9 | ROUTE: Start over the bones on the left bank, glide out to the animals wading in the stream, then follow the current around the mossy hump toward the distant lit cave opening. | FAULTS: The bones are conspicuously arranged in the corner; several animals repeat the same rump-up, head-down pose, and some submerged legs are hard to separate from the water.
v5 | PHOTO | PLACE 10 | ROUTE: Descend from the grassy lip to the cracked dark rock shelf, skim the foam along the stepped cliff bases, then push toward the offshore-facing ledge where the wave bursts upward. | FAULTS: none.
v6 | PAINTING | PLACE 4 | ROUTE: Fly up to the nearest giant vertebra, dip beside its waterfall, then follow the line of cliff tops into the cloud bank. | FAULTS: The same upright vertebra silhouette and round face repeat at suspiciously regular intervals; waterfall after waterfall drops from nearly identical ledges with no visible catchment, and clouds hide how the cliff bases connect.
v7 | FILM | PLACE 8 | ROUTE: Follow the shallow rivulet past the veined glowing sacs, close on the animal at the next cluster, then arc right up to the lit cave mouth. | FAULTS: The same green-lit mounds recur at regular-looking intervals; the cave mouth reads like a black cutout with lights parked just inside, with little readable interior behind them.
v8 | PHOTO | PLACE 8 | ROUTE: Lift off the dark foreground ridge, drop low over the nearest glacier crevasses, then cross the ice toward the banded rock bluff on the far side. | FAULTS: The heavy blue cast crushes shadow detail in the near rocks and makes the distant glacier read more like a single textured sheet than broken terrain.
RANK: v2, v5, v4, v1, v8, v7, v3, v6.

close4 | WIDE wide3 | SURE 9 | WHERE: Low at the waterline beside the right-hand drinking animal, looking diagonally left across it toward the central raised-headed adult and calf. | MATCHES: Raised-headed gray adult facing left with a small calf at its right; right foreground animal drinking; blunt elongated heads with diagonal facial slits, wrinkled hides and thick legs; waterfall upper left, red-canopy tree behind, wet pebble bank and diffuse upper-left daylight. | BREAKS: Pale growths and insects on the foreground animal's back are not distinguishable in the wide; no definite contradiction, but individual identity of that drinking animal is less secure than the adult/calf grouping.

crit.text:
close1 | WIDE wide1 | SURE 8 | WHERE: Low at water level in the mid-left shallow wading flats, looking ahead toward the upper-left sun, distant steam plume, and upper-right cliff cave. | MATCHES: Low golden sun at upper left, tall white steam plume on left plain, stepped snow-streaked cliff with huge mist-filled cave arch at upper right, white sinter rock with red feathery shrubs, shallow reflective water, and pale four-legged eyeless creatures with long necks and pink filament heads. | BREAKS: Wading creatures change count, positions, and poses from wide1's mid-left cluster (center four-legged creature raises a dripping head and lifts a hind leg, right creature dips right instead of standing tall facing left, and a fourth creature lies half-submerged in mist behind left); the raised steaming bone-pit mound with tall red bushes to the right is replaced by low white boulders with small scrub; and the distant cliff cave and steam plume retain almost the exact 2D framing of wide1 despite moving forward-left.
close2 | WIDE wide2 | SURE 8 | WHERE: Midground center on the dark valley floor just downstream and left of the feeding creature, looking up-valley toward the orange left horizon and upper-right glowing cave. | MATCHES: Dark twilight cloud deck with orange horizon glow at far left, dark cliff wall with green bioluminescent cave pods at upper right, distant glowing pods at far left, dark volcanic gravel, and stocky four-legged dark wrinkled creature with thin hanging tail and pale flank marking feeding head-down at a green-glowing veined pod. | BREAKS: The creature's flank marking changes from broader pale shoulder-and-hip patches in wide2 to one sharp vertical white stripe at mid-back, with slimy webbing added around its four ankles; the pod it eats morphs from a modest rounded dome with a dark right cap into a giant multi-ribbed segmented sac extending off frame right; and the rocky stream channel running immediately left and in front of the creature in wide2 vanishes into dry gravel with a tiny puddle.
close3 | WIDE wide1 | SURE 9 | WHERE: On the right-foreground white sinter terrace just in front of the dead creature on the rim of the steaming bone-lined sinkhole, looking slightly left across the rim toward the sun, steam plume, and cliff cave. | MATCHES: Steaming sinkhole lined with the same curved giant fossil ribs and fallen angular rock block on the right, dense red feathery shrubs on the back-left rim, pale four-legged pink-filament carcass lying on the rock shelf (head left, four cloven-hooved legs right) with a live four-legged creature standing behind it on the rim, upper-left sun and steam plume, distant left waders, and upper-right cliff cave. | BREAKS: The standing four-legged creature's neck arches downward over the pit with limp hanging filaments instead of reaching high upward-right as in wide1; the carcass's four legs lie neatly parallel further forward with a loose bone fragment added beside them; and the wide turquoise foreground stream channel and four nearby mid-left waders immediately left of the pit terrace in wide1 are missing or flattened into sunlit glare.
close4 | WIDE wide3 | SURE 7 | WHERE: Low at water level near the center-right river channel, looking left and slightly upstream toward the central gravel bar, standing adult and calf, tree ferns, red-canopied tree, and upper-left waterfall. | MATCHES: Multi-tiered waterfall on mossy cliff at upper left, slender red-canopied tree and tree ferns on left bank, shallow cobble river, and grey-brown thick-skinned four-legged trunkless creatures including a profile adult facing left on the gravel bar with a small calf at its feet and a river wader with snout submerged. | BREAKS: Both the foreground-right river wader and the small calf beside the standing adult flip 180 degrees to face left instead of right as in wide3; the recumbent adult lying on the gravel bank left of the standing adult and the tall bare dead snag tree behind it are missing; the standing adult has water streaming from its mouth; and six prominent vertical gill slits appear on each creature's neck along with white bulbous back growths and swarming flies on the foreground wader not visible in wide3.
close5 | WIDE wide3 | SURE 8 | WHERE: Macro low-angle on the bottom-left mossy riverbank right behind the decaying bones and pale puffball sacs, looking right across the river toward the waterfall, cavern arch, herd, and distant bright cave exit. | MATCHES: Overarching limestone cavern roof leading to the misty tunnel and bright far-right exit, waterfall and red foliage at upper left, mossy leaf-litter bank with decaying bones, pale spherical puffball sacs and a ruptured cup-shaped sac, and herd of four-legged grey-brown trunkless creatures wading in the rocky river. | BREAKS: The fern-covered natural stone arch on the midground right bank loses its open arch gap and becomes a solid green mound; foreground props change (an upturned lower jawbone with flat molar teeth appears at bottom right, three smooth white puffballs change into one water-beaded globe with beetles plus a dark shriveled sac, and the repositioned open cup sprays golden spores); and the large closest wading creature in the center-left foreground river of wide3 vanishes.
close6 | WIDE wide2 | SURE 8 | WHERE: Low on the right bank of the foreground stream right beside the large red-veined glowing dome, looking up-valley along the stream toward the midground feeding creature, orange left horizon, and upper-right glowing cave. | MATCHES: Twilight sky with orange horizon band at upper left, dark cliff and green-glowing cave mouth at upper right, shallow rocky stream reflecting green light on left, midground four-legged dark creature feeding at a glowing pod, and large foreground translucent red-veined green-glowing dome on the right with small flying insects. | BREAKS: Three neighbouring foreground pods in wide2—the dark deflated dome in front and both the split glowing green orb and tall pale ribbed sac sitting directly between the hero dome and the stream—completely vanish so the hero dome sits alone on the bank with root-like tendrils; and a large curled four-limbed fetus with a cloven forehoof is clearly visible inside the dome (plus white moths perched outside), whereas the backlit dome in wide2 looks milky and empty.
wide1 | PLACE MOSTLY | FIX: Rebuild close1 with true 3D parallax so moving down to the mid-left wading pool shifts the distant cliff-and-plume backdrop and preserves the raised red-bush bone-pit mound on the right.
wide2 | PLACE MOSTLY | FIX: Restore the rocky stream channel running past the left side of the midground feeding creature in close2 and match its small rounded pod instead of replacing them with dry gravel and a giant ribbed sac.
wide3 | PLACE MOSTLY | FIX: Fix the central river-bar staging in close4 where the calf and river wader flip 180 degrees to face left and both the recumbent adult and tall dead snag tree behind them vanish.

close3 | WIDE wide1 | SURE 9 | WHERE: On the right-foreground white sinter terrace just in front of the dead creature on the rim of the steaming bone-lined sinkhole, looking slightly left across the rim toward the sun, steam plume, and cliff cave. | MATCHES: Steaming sinkhole lined with the same curved giant fossil ribs and fallen angular rock block on the right, dense red feathery shrubs on the back-left rim, pale four-legged pink-filament carcass lying on the rock shelf (head left, four cloven-hooved legs right) with a live four-legged creature standing behind it on the rim, upper-left sun and steam plume, distant left waders, and upper-right cliff cave. | BREAKS: The standing four-legged creature's neck arches downward over the pit with limp hanging filaments instead of reaching high upward-right as in wide1; the carcass's four legs lie neatly parallel further forward with a loose bone fragment added beside them; and the wide turquoise foreground stream channel and four nearby mid-left waders immediately left of the pit terrace in wide1 are missing or flattened into sunlit glare.
close4 | WIDE wide3 | SURE 7 | WHERE: Low at water level near the center-right river channel, looking left and slightly upstream toward the central gravel bar, standing adult and calf, tree ferns, red-canopied tree, and upper-left waterfall. | MATCHES: Multi-tiered waterfall on mossy cliff at upper left, slender red-canopied tree and tree ferns on left bank, shallow cobble river, and grey-brown thick-skinned four-legged trunkless creatures including a profile adult facing left on the gravel bar with a small calf at its feet and a river wader with snout submerged. | BREAKS: Both the foreground-right river wader and the small calf beside the standing adult flip 180 degrees to face left instead of right as in wide3; the recumbent adult lying on the gravel bank left of the standing adult and the tall bare dead snag tree behind it are missing; the standing adult has water streaming from its mouth; and six prominent vertical gill slits appear on each creature's neck along with white bulbous back growths and swarming flies on the foreground wader not visible in wide3.
close5 | WIDE wide3 | SURE 8 | WHERE: Macro low-angle on the bottom-left mossy riverbank right behind the decaying bones and pale puffball sacs, looking right across the river toward the waterfall, cavern arch, herd, and distant bright cave exit. | MATCHES: Overarching limestone cavern roof leading to the misty tunnel and bright far-right exit, waterfall and red foliage at upper left, mossy leaf-litter bank with decaying bones, pale spherical puffball sacs and a ruptured cup-shaped sac, and herd of four-legged grey-brown trunkless creatures wading in the rocky river. | BREAKS: The fern-covered natural stone arch on the midground right bank loses its open arch gap and becomes a solid green mound; foreground props change (an upturned lower jawbone with flat molar teeth appears at bottom right, three smooth white puffballs change into one water-beaded globe with beetles plus a dark shriveled sac, and the repositioned open cup sprays golden spores); and the large closest wading creature in the center-left foreground river of wide3 vanishes.
close6 | WIDE wide2 | SURE 8 | WHERE: Low on the right bank of the foreground stream right beside the large red-veined glowing dome, looking up-valley along the stream toward the midground feeding creature, orange left horizon, and upper-right glowing cave. | MATCHES: Twilight sky with orange horizon band at upper left, dark cliff and green-glowing cave mouth at upper right, shallow rocky stream reflecting green light on left, midground four-legged dark creature feeding at a glowing pod, and large foreground translucent red-veined green-glowing dome on the right with small flying insects. | BREAKS: Three neighbouring foreground pods in wide2—the dark deflated dome in front and both the split glowing green orb and tall pale ribbed sac sitting directly between the hero dome and the stream—completely vanish so the hero dome sits alone on the bank with root-like tendrils; and a large curled four-limbed fetus with a cloven forehoof is clearly visible inside the dome (plus white moths perched outside), whereas the backlit dome in wide2 looks milky and empty.

--- FIRST REPLY ---
close1 | WIDE wide1 | SURE 9 | WHERE: Low in the shallow flats left of the foreground sinkhole, looking across the feeding animals toward the same distant cliff; sinkhole falls outside the right edge. | MATCHES: Long dark cliff recess upper right; stepped pale ridge; tall steam plume on left; warm upper-left sun reflected in shallow water; pale four-legged animals with long necks ending in pink tentacle fans; red scrub on pale slabs. | BREAKS: No definite contradiction; the three foreground animals cannot be individually identified in the wide, so their exact positions are not proven.
close2 | WIDE wide2 | SURE 9 | WHERE: At ground level beside the middle-distance feeding adult and its glowing pod cluster, looking toward the right-hand cliff while retaining the valley opening on the left. | MATCHES: Dark heavy quadruped with pale transverse back bands, short tail and lowered blunt head; green glowing ribbed membranes with red veins; low orange sunset strip on left; same cliff cave with green-lit contents upper right; dark gravel and wet ground. | BREAKS: Fine pale webbing binding the feet is newly visible but not resolvable in the wide; no definite anatomical or geographic contradiction.
close3 | WIDE wide1 | SURE 10 | WHERE: On the near sinkhole lip, moved forward and lowered beside the prone animal, looking along the lip toward the standing animal and the distant cliff. | MATCHES: Same prone pale animal with pink fan head to left and long folded legs to right; standing fan-headed animal farther along the lip; red branching shrubs opposite; curved pale horizontal sinkhole ribs; large fallen angular slab against the inner wall; same distant cliff recess, steam and warm left-hand light. | BREAKS: Standing animal has lowered its neck relative to the wide, a pose change rather than a design change; no fixed-landmark contradiction.
close4 | WIDE wide3 | SURE 9 | WHERE: Low at the waterline beside the right-hand drinking animal, looking diagonally left across it toward the central raised-headed adult and calf. | MATCHES: Raised-headed gray adult facing left with a small calf at its right; right foreground animal drinking; blunt elongated heads with diagonal facial slits, wrinkled hides and thick legs; waterfall upper left, red-canopy tree behind, wet pebble bank and diffuse upper-left daylight. | BREAKS: Pale growths and insects on the foreground animal's back are not distinguishable in the wide; no definite contradiction, but individual identity of that drinking animal is less secure than the adult/calf grouping.
close5 | WIDE wide3 | SURE 10 | WHERE: Almost on the ground beside the bone-and-sphere heap at the extreme lower-left bank, looking across the heap toward the stream and right-hand tunnel. | MATCHES: Cream translucent round bodies, collapsed brownish sphere, broken open shell, large pale curved bones among wet leaves and moss; waterfall left, red-leaved trees, overhead stone arch, distant bright tunnel opening right and gray animals in the stream. | BREAKS: Foreground toothed jaw is much clearer and more prominent than in the wide, but the wide's heap is too small and partly overlapped to establish a conflicting bone arrangement; no definite contradiction.
close6 | WIDE wide2 | SURE 10 | WHERE: Ground level immediately beside the huge foreground pod on the right bank, looking obliquely along its stream-facing skin and back down the valley. | MATCHES: Giant translucent green-lit dome with branching red veins and dark membrane skirt; stream running along its left side; banded feeding adult and smaller pod cluster farther left; same green-lit cliff cave, dark bare rock and narrow orange sunset under blue-gray cloud. | BREAKS: A curled hoofed fetus is now visible through the membrane where the wide only shows a cloudy luminous surface; this is a new revelation, not evidence of changed pod contents. No definite geographic contradiction.
wide1 | PLACE YES | FIX: No demonstrated spatial break; preserve the standing sinkhole animal's neck pose if these are meant to be literally simultaneous frames.
wide2 | PLACE YES | FIX: No demonstrated spatial break; carry enough fetal silhouette into the wide's foreground pod to make the close6 reveal visibly continuous rather than newly invented.
wide3 | PLACE YES | FIX: No demonstrated spatial break; retain a recognizable arrangement of the same bones and spheres when cutting from the wide to close5.

--- SECOND REPLY ---
close1 | WIDE wide1 | SURE 9 | WHERE: Low in the shallow flats left of the sinkhole, looking across the feeding herd toward the same distant cliff. | MATCHES: Dark cliff recess upper right, stepped pale ridge, tall left-hand steam plume, low warm light from left, reflective wet slabs, red scrub, pale four-legged stock with pink neck-tip fans. | BREAKS: No fixed-landmark break; the foreground feeding group cannot be matched individual for individual, and its raised animal should not be confused with the one on the dry sinkhole rim.
close2 | WIDE wide2 | SURE 9 | WHERE: Low beside the midground animal and pod cluster, looking toward the right-hand cliff and keeping the valley opening on the left. | MATCHES: Dark four-legged stock with pale transverse back marking and lowered head, green-lit ribbed membranes, dark wet gravel, orange left horizon and green-lit cliff cave upper right. | BREAKS: No definite break; webbing around the feet and narrower stripe contours cannot be checked at wide scale.
close3 | WIDE wide1 | SURE 10 | WHERE: Just inside the wide's near-right rock shelf, low beside the prone animal and aimed along the sinkhole lip. | MATCHES: Prone fan-headed body with head left and legs right, standing animal beyond it, red shrubs, layered curved pit ribs, angular slab in the wall, steam, same cliff recess and upper-left light. | BREAKS: The standing animal's neck is upright in the wide but hooked down over the pit here; a real pose discontinuity if simultaneous.
close4 | WIDE wide3 | SURE 8 | WHERE: Low in the shallows near the center-right drinker, looking past it toward the central raised-head adult and calf. | MATCHES: Raised-head adult faces left with calf at its right, blunt slit-marked heads and thick legs, waterfall upper left, red tree, pebbled shallows and diffuse daylight. | BREAKS: The likely center-right drinker has its head screen-right in the wide but projects screen-left here; a different individual or substantial angle change is possible but its same-moment blocking is not clear. Pale growths on its back are unresolved in the wide.
close5 | WIDE wide3 | SURE 9 | WHERE: Ground-level at the extreme lower-left bone pile, looking just over the stream toward the waterfall and right tunnel. | MATCHES: Pale spheres, crumpled sphere, broken shell and bones among wet foliage; waterfall, red canopies, overhead arch, right tunnel glint and herd. | BREAKS: The separate medium intact sphere between the crumpled sphere and broken shell in the wide is not plainly present in the close; a conspicuous toothed jaw dominates the close but is not identifiable in the wide. Angle and overlap may account for part of this.
close6 | WIDE wide2 | SURE 10 | WHERE: Immediately beside the huge right-bank pod, looking along its stream-facing membrane down the valley. | MATCHES: Green dome with branching red veins, membrane skirt, stream on left, feeding adult at a smaller pod, green cave and orange sunset under blue-gray cloud. | BREAKS: none; the fetus and individual insects are revealed at this distance, rather than established as missing in the wide.
wide1 | PLACE YES | FIX: Match the sinkhole animal's neck pose across the simultaneous cut.
wide2 | PLACE YES | FIX: No proven break; keep the fetal silhouette consistent through the big pod's changing translucency.
wide3 | PLACE MOSTLY | FIX: Match the center-right drinker's heading and identify it unambiguously across the cut.

close5 | WIDE wide3 | SURE 8 | WHERE: at ground level in the egg and bone pile on the lower-left bank of wide3, looking right and in toward the river, the herd and the lit tunnel opening under the arch | MATCHES: round white eggs, one of them broken open; long pale bones; moss and leaf litter; waterfall upper centre-left; red-leaved tree to its left; bare branching tree; huge cave arch across the top right; bright tunnel opening at the far right; river with grey creatures wading; misty shafts of light | BREAKS: a toothed jawbone in the foreground that is not in the wide3 bone pile; a stream of golden spores or dust rising from the broken egg, absent in wide3; one egg is a wrinkled, collapsed, translucent sac unlike the solid eggs in wide3; the herd is smaller and sparser, and the head-up adult and calf are missing
close6 | WIDE wide2 | SURE 8 | WHERE: low beside the large veined pod in the right foreground of wide2, looking left and up the valley along the creek toward the grazer and its pod, with the cave on the right wall | MATCHES: large translucent pod with red veins and small moths on it; creek running left of the pod; grazer feeding at a glowing pod in the midground; green-glowing cave mouth in the right-hand cliff; orange sunset under purple cloud at upper left; dark mud and rocks; mist; dusk light | BREAKS: a clearly visible embryo of the grazer species inside the pod, never seen in any pod in wide2; slimy webbing strands spreading from the pod base; the cave appears closer to the valley floor and nearer than its high-wall position in wide2
wide1 | PLACE YES | FIX: in close3 the standing creature's head is hanging to the ground and the sinkhole ledges have become giant ribs; match wide1, with the head raised high on a curved neck and stone strata at the rim
wide2 | PLACE MOSTLY | FIX: in close2 the pod the grazer is feeding on is a huge, torn, deflated sac; wide2 shows a small, intact, ribbed pod about the animal's size with the creek beside it
wide3 | PLACE MOSTLY | FIX: close4 drops the giant cave arch completely and puts eggs on an animal's back; restore the overhanging arch on the right and keep the eggs only in the ground bone pile

crit.text:
v1 | FILM | PLACE 9 | ROUTE: Skim the foreground water channel, bank past the long-legged animal on the steaming sinkhole rim, then cross the flats toward the enormous cave in the escarpment. | FAULTS: Several waders repeat the same head-down silhouette; their needle-thin feet and the prone animal’s splayed limbs are hard to read against the rock.
v2 | PHOTO | PLACE 10 | ROUTE: Drop past the nearer left flowstone to the lit boulders beside the tiny caver, climb around the central stalagmite cluster, then peer into the dark passage to its right. | FAULTS: none.
v3 | AMATEUR | PLACE 6 | ROUTE: Slip between the close icy trunks, track beside the bison-like herd crossing the glade, then drift into the faint trees behind it. | FAULTS: The two sides frame the sky almost symmetrically; bark shines like clear plastic, the herd repeats in side profile, and the uniform mist turns the deeper woods into a backdrop.
v4 | FILM | PLACE 9 | ROUTE: Start over the bones on the left bank, glide out to the animals wading in the stream, then follow the current around the mossy hump toward the distant lit cave opening. | FAULTS: The bones are conspicuously arranged in the corner; several animals repeat the same rump-up, head-down pose, and some submerged legs are hard to separate from the water.
v5 | PHOTO | PLACE 10 | ROUTE: Descend from the grassy lip to the cracked dark rock shelf, skim the foam along the stepped cliff bases, then push toward the offshore-facing ledge where the wave bursts upward. | FAULTS: none.
v6 | PAINTING | PLACE 4 | ROUTE: Fly up to the nearest giant vertebra, dip beside its waterfall, then follow the line of cliff tops into the cloud bank. | FAULTS: The same upright vertebra silhouette and round face repeat at suspiciously regular intervals; waterfall after waterfall drops from nearly identical ledges with no visible catchment, and clouds hide how the cliff bases connect.
v7 | FILM | PLACE 8 | ROUTE: Follow the shallow rivulet past the veined glowing sacs, close on the animal at the next cluster, then arc right up to the lit cave mouth. | FAULTS: The same green-lit mounds recur at regular-looking intervals; the cave mouth reads like a black cutout with lights parked just inside, with little readable interior behind them.
v8 | PHOTO | PLACE 8 | ROUTE: Lift off the dark foreground ridge, drop low over the nearest glacier crevasses, then cross the ice toward the banded rock bluff on the far side. | FAULTS: The heavy blue cast crushes shadow detail in the near rocks and makes the distant glacier read more like a single textured sheet than broken terrain.

pb1f-t1.what: frame 1 plate for the corrected master (master-x4): as pb1-e but with no cloud; standards orb-iss44-sinai.jpg + orb-iss47-brandberg.jpg; take 1

pb1f-t2.what: frame 1 plate for the corrected master (master-x4): as pb1-e but with no cloud; standards orb-iss44-sinai.jpg + orb-iss47-brandberg.jpg; take 2

A-establishing.reason: Reads as location photography of a cave you could walk into: river route, bones, herd, fallen ring and second skylight at four distances. Herd matches the detail view after one revision of A-est-t53.
A-establishing.faults: Bone pile in the corner looks arranged; several animals share a head-down pose; the arch is too clean; herd about 1.4 times larger in frame than in t53; most Earth-like of the three.

A-detail-1.reason: Bladders venting gold dust on the bones, with the herd, the fallen ring and the far skylight soft behind: the kill told in one frame.
A-detail-1.faults: Made from A-est-t53, so the soft herd behind predates the herd revision; toothed jaw and venting bladder are not in the wide pile; fallen ring reads as a mound.

A-detail-2.reason: Eyeless long-necked grazers drinking, bladders and flies already on one back; the design the wide herd was revised to match.
A-detail-2.faults: Arch not visible; drinker heading differs from the wide; lying adult and dead tree missing.

B-establishing.reason: Landform carries the frame: tide channel, airway shaft with ruined hoops, flats and cliff cave at four distances; heavy vapour; waders small and scattered.
B-establishing.faults: Far waders repeat a head-down silhouette; red plumes sit slightly on top of the rock; vapour plumes a little evenly spaced; cave soft.

B-detail-1.reason: One-step revision of B-d1-t32 after blind packet 12: carcass collapsed and untidy with a stain under it, legs no longer parallel, standing wader less stiff; same positions as the wide.
B-detail-1.faults: Not re-tested blind; standing wader still shows three legs from this angle; hoops read more like bone than in the wide.

B-detail-2.reason: One-step revision of B-d2-t20 after blind packet 13: skin reads as real hide, wet clumped tendrils, no bead-line drip; same three animals in the same places.
B-detail-2.faults: Not re-tested blind; tendril tufts are browner than the pink of the wide; fourth animal lying in the water has no match in the wide.

C-establishing.reason: Dusk valley with three sac colonies along the stream, the banded animal at the middle colony and the lit cave; glows now light the water and wet ground after one revision of C-est-t50.
C-establishing.faults: Lit sacs recur at regular-looking intervals; cave reads as a dark opening with lights parked inside; far glow a little painted; animal small.

C-detail-1.reason: What the light is for: a young banded animal inside the veined sac, hoof against the membrane, the stream, the middle colony and the cave behind.
C-detail-1.faults: Made from C-est-t50, so its moths are pale where the revised wide has dull ones; neighbouring sacs of the near colony are missing; nothing can be seen inside the sac in the wide.

C-detail-2.reason: The snare: banded animal with its snout in the ribbed sac, threads round fore and hind legs, lit cave behind.
C-detail-2.faults: Sac larger and more torn than in the wide; stream beside it missing; band is one stripe here and broader patches in the wide.

ribs-establishing.reason: Two facing rows of rib blades curving in over a tidal flat: reads as a cage you walk through; weed line, drowned carcass, kite-wings and far surf at four distances.
ribs-establishing.faults: More designed than the other places; the returning bore is only a thin surf line; two near kite-wings run in the same pose.

heart-establishing.reason: Reads as a real lava lake at dusk: bench route on the left, crust-walkers at three distances, the vessel mouth and its lava fall, the buttress, the foundered walker.
heart-establishing.faults: The five mid-distance walkers share a silhouette; near walker body is thin and sketchy; second chamber beyond the buttress is only a glow.

marsh-establishing.reason: Vein channel as the route, bubbling seep pool with steam, stalk colonies, wallowers, and the salt-crusted dead with one still alive on the thin crust, under flat white overcast with a rain curtain.
marsh-establishing.faults: Gas domes in the pool look a little like smooth eggs; stalk fans resemble red palm fronds; far flats repeat small clusters.

spine-establishing.reason: Blade spire with burned tip and streaming tether-kites, tracks leading to the canal mouth, the ridge of spires receding with a strike on the third, cloud sea and one line of orange.
spine-establishing.faults: The most dramatic and so the closest to a poster; lightning a touch too violet and clean; far spires small.

eye-establishing.reason: Round lake with amber radial shallows and a black centre carrying one set of rings, the brow overhang on the right, the herd at the near shore, the outflow at the bottom.
eye-establishing.faults: Herd animals are small and a little alike; the shallows-to-deep edge is softer on the left; outflow stream is cut by the frame.

heart-detail-1.reason: The line itself: sulphur crack steaming on the solid bench, an open seam, a walker stepping out, the lava fall behind.
heart-detail-1.faults: Foreground focus is shallow enough to hint at a tilt-shift miniature; the walkers repeat one silhouette.

heart-detail-2.reason: Two legs arched out of the crust, the body already under folded lava skin, living walkers feeding behind it.
heart-detail-2.faults: The far walkers are near-copies of each other.

heart-detail-3.reason: Three walkers at a bright seam, the feeding trunk fraying into tendrils in the lava, the fall and the buttress behind.
heart-detail-3.faults: The middle walker's lifted foot ends in a flat disc that looks designed.

heart-detail-4.reason: The vessel mouth lit from below, the fall braiding down the scree, two walkers at its foot for scale.
heart-detail-4.faults: The bright seam along the bottom edge is out of focus and a little graphic.

marsh-detail-1.reason: A dome of gas about to break, a burst beside it, the salt rim in front, stalks and a wallower behind.
marsh-detail-1.faults: The dome is very clean, close to glass.

marsh-detail-2.reason: Salt-crusted stalks with crimson fans dripping, small winged insects round them, one stalk cut off dead, a wallower and a seep mound behind.
marsh-detail-2.faults: Reads a little like a palm from far off.

marsh-detail-3.reason: An adult and a calf rooting with tusk-like feelers, one more submerged, red water to the belly, no eyes.
marsh-detail-3.faults: Close to a walrus crossed with a tardigrade: the least alien animal in the set.

marsh-detail-4.reason: One alive and sunk to the shoulders in grey mud through broken crust, two salt-crusted dead beside it, the living herd in the channel behind. Take 2 kept because take 1 gave the animal an eye.
marsh-detail-4.faults: The front-left salt mound is out of focus and large in the frame.

eye-detail-1.reason: Adults and a calf drinking at the shore, eyeless tapering heads, rings spreading, far cliffs.
eye-detail-1.faults: Anatomy is close to a camelid; the right-hand animal is cut by the frame and soft.

eye-detail-2.reason: Amber filaments under clear water, threads of small bubbles, and a full-size drinker at mid-distance so the lake reads at real scale. Single-step fix of the redo eye-d2b-t2, whose drinker read as a horse: it is now the lean, earless, eyeless drinker of detail 1.
eye-detail-2.faults: The drinker's body is still close to a thin horse or camelid. First attempt (eye-d2-t1, t2) dropped: thumb-sized grazers read as miniature lambs.

eye-detail-3.reason: The shelf ends, a submerged cliff drops into blue-black, pale forms hang in the deep, a skeleton lies at the edge. Take 2 kept because take 1 puts a skull with an eye socket in front of eyeless animals.
eye-detail-3.faults: The skeleton is small and its head is hard to read.

eye-detail-4.reason: The water domes at the centre and thin pale spines break the surface in a ring; two drinkers watch. Single-step fix of eye-d4-t1, whose drinkers had ears and wool: they are now the bare-skinned, earless drinkers of detail 1.
eye-detail-4.faults: What rises is only hinted at. Seen from behind and out of focus, the blunt earless heads read as plain stumps.

spine-detail-1.reason: A ridge-runner dead on the snow, rimed, a burn down its flank, bare scorched rock under it; the first spire with the tunnel mouth and tracks behind, lightning beyond.
spine-detail-1.faults: The ice slab at bottom right is soft and large.

spine-detail-2.reason: Translucent ribbons streaming from stalks anchored in cone-like holdfasts on the lee face, rime on the windward face, far spires.
spine-detail-2.faults: The largest ribbon is close to a torn plastic sheet.

spine-detail-3.reason: The bolt on the spire tip, sparks and steam, kites lit from inside, far spires and the orange horizon.
spine-detail-3.faults: The left foreground rock is a large soft mass; the most poster-like frame of the details.

spine-detail-4.reason: The herd packed against the wall inside the canal, one standing at the mouth, ice on the roof, kites and the next spire outside.
spine-detail-4.faults: The animals are close to shaggy dogs with tendril faces; the ice floor is very clean.

ribs-detail-1.reason: A drowned long-legged animal hanging head down in the weed with small pale crabs on it, water still running off, older bones higher up, rib blades behind.
ribs-detail-1.faults: The second skeleton above it is very neat.

ribs-detail-2.reason: Kite-wings wading; one pulls a worm from a pool with its tendril head, another shakes off water, surf and rib blades behind. Single-step fix of ribs-d3-t2: the near animal's eye is gone, so its head is the same blind tuft of tendrils as the others.
ribs-detail-2.faults: The far flier is soft and its wing is very orange; the foreground weed takes the lower quarter of the frame.

ribs-detail-3.reason: Ledges crowded with kite-wings above the weed line, white streaks down the rock, orange crust, one landing.
ribs-detail-3.faults: Two blurred fliers in the foreground take a lot of the frame.

ribs-detail-4.reason: A wall of white water coming through between two ribs, kite-wings lifting off ahead of it.
ribs-detail-4.faults: The kite-wings fly in an even line; the wave is closer to storm surf than to a single bore.

breath-detail-1.reason: Three waders feeding in the channel against the low sun, legs planted in the water, the cliff behind. One-step revision of the step 1 detail B-d2-t20: real bare hide, and the tidy lines of drips are gone.
breath-detail-1.faults: The left animal is cut by the frame and soft. Adopted by eye and not blind-tested; the step 1 blind scores apply to the earlier B-d2-t20.

breath-detail-2.reason: The rim: the last one that came to it lying collapsed on the rock, a living wader standing over the drop with its head down, plumes rooted in the cracks, the ruined hoops in the shaft. One-step revision of the step 1 detail B-d1-t32: untidier carcass, real bare skin, uneven vapour.
breath-detail-2.faults: The carcass is centred and evenly lit, which still reads a little staged. Adopted by eye and not blind-tested; the step 1 blind scores apply to the earlier B-d1-t32.

breath-detail-3.reason: Crimson feathered plumes rooted on the lip, dripping, a bone at the root, a wader in the fog behind, vapour leaving the shaft.
breath-detail-3.faults: Close to a red seaweed or a conifer branch.

breath-detail-4.reason: Looking down the shaft: cartilage hoops, a slab fallen across them, vapour filling it, shelf and waders beyond.
breath-detail-4.faults: The depth of the shaft is hidden by the vapour; the plume at left is soft and large.

breath-establishing.reason: Step 1 establishing view of direction B, carried into the full set unchanged. Landform carries the frame: tide channel, airway shaft with ruined hoops, flats and cliff cave at four distances; heavy vapour; waders small and scattered.
breath-establishing.faults: Far waders repeat a head-down silhouette; red plumes sit slightly on top of the rock; vapour plumes a little evenly spaced; cave soft.

reveal-rejected.reason: Reads as an astronaut photograph at real scale: limb, cloud fields with shadows, a cyclone, sunglint; skull with the eye lake, spine range, ribs as curved ridges and capes, the red delta, the caldera plume, the arm.
reveal-rejected.faults: Skull and hand are very literal; ribs partly lost under cloud on the right; pelvis and legs fade into haze and barely read.

reveal-frame-1.reason: Key frame 1, just above the lake: the round shore fills the frame. The plate pb1e-t1, graded to its window of the master. SCALE test (bo1 to bo3): real terrain 3 of 3.
reveal-frame-1.faults: Read as 10 to 60 km wide against 250 km stated. A critic calls it 'vulnerable to macro/model' reads. Its mist plume, cliff wall and whitecaps are softer in frame 2.

reveal-frame-2.reason: Key frame 2, the skull massif: head from e3-HD-t4 drawn through the head warp, sea and throat from pb2g-t2. HEAD test (ca1 to ca3): skull or screaming face with the lake as an eye 3 of 3.
reveal-frame-2.faults: The weakest frame for scale: read as 40 to 150 km wide against 920 km stated; one of three chose 'a painting or drawing'; round pits and lace-like texture called 'possibly artificial or miniature'.

reveal-frame-3.reason: Key frame 3, head and shoulders: a window of master-x6. SCALE test (bz1 to bz3): real terrain 2 of 3, no fish read.
reveal-frame-3.faults: Read as 100 to 300 km wide against 2,150 km stated. Several orange dots where frame 4 shows one. Sea beside the crown stretched up to 1.58 times by the head warp.

reveal-frame-4.reason: Key frame 4, the reveal frame: the whole titan from orbit, a window of master-x6 (98.7% of its width). GLANCE 3 of 3, FULL 6 of 6, STATE 4, 4, 4, PLACES 6, 5 and 6 of 6 (bu1 to by3).
reveal-frame-4.faults: Every viewer says skeleton. 3 of 6 call it a digital illustration. Waist reads too long 3 of 3; legs short, hands big, feet small. Red channels read as blood or dye. Storm 'puffy'. The body does not foreshorten with the planet's curve.
